¶1 Irfan 08

¶2 Bismillah hir rahma nir raheem

¶3 We dealt with theoretical Irfan we dealt with some aspects of practical Irfan in the sense that how the mystic describes the journey. Now we'll come to some practical advice from the mystics how this journey should be carried out, now the journey is usually called sulook which is translated in English as way farer and sulook in Arabic means to say the past and therefore, the behavior is also called sulook because it is how you move around as a personality and thats your sulook, your behavior. The person who does sulook is called saalik, a way farer, someone who actually travels through these practical stages to reach the real goal of mysticism which is knowledge of course it is a different perspective that mystics have.

¶4 Now, in this first of all, we should know that in the sulook we are not traveling from one place to another place. We are actually finding ourselves, it is a journey inside rather than journey outside, it is concentrating on one capability on ones disk.. that Allah has given them and then through it finding what's going on around us. In fact, now that you're sitting in this room, there are many things going on around which will not see and the purpose of this journey is to see what's going on and to see the presence of God to see our own selves. And these all would actually urge us to, to concentrate on our own soul, as we said, at the beginning of the course that whoever knows that knows their soul, they will know the Lord they will know the reality they would get knowledge and everything which is inside our soul.

¶5 So let's start with an advice from Shaikh Najmuddin kubra which is a mystic of the seventh century Islamic calendar and he is the founder of the of the Tariqa which is called kubrawiyyah after his name kubra. He is called Kubra because people saw him as a tremendous reminder of Allah (swt) after the verse fa-izaa jaaa'atit taaam matul kubraa.(sura 79; ayat 34) and that's why he's called kubra because kubra usually is name of, is actively for muannas, ladies. For men, we say akbar, he is called kubra because of course, of the verse. Now, Shaikh Najmuddin ‘O slave of Allah, know that you are a wayfarer saalik seeking your lord and ultimately one day you would meet him, as said in a tradition, whoever hopes to meet God should know that the time of the meeting will come.

¶6 Now of course, I don't know why there is a mistake in this quotation or maybe he has somehow confused because this is a verse of the Quran. That's faman kaana yarjoo liqaaa'a Rabbihee falya'mal 'amalan saalihanw wa laa yushrik bi'ibaadati Rabbiheee ahadaa (sura 18:ayat110) This is a verse from the Quran tradition. So whoever hopes to meet the Lord should know that one day they would meet the Lord and whoever doesn't hope should know as well that they are going to meet but in an embarrassing situation. And you should know that God the Exalted by perfect might and wisdom has distinct two journeys for the children of Adam one of them is involuntary qahri and the other one is voluntary, ikhtiyari.

¶7 In fact, he is trying to say that this journey that you're setting out to travel is something that you would naturally go through when you die, you would meet the lord, you would see his presence. However, when you die and when you go through all those stages and the stations of barzakh and Qiyamah , it is something out of your control. You go through it in a qahri way, in an involuntary way, and at the end you come to the Lord. He says there is a shortcut to this, this is actually a route which you voluntarily go a path that you voluntary go and that is the mystical way the sulook. Now, why should we reach if eventually we are going to go through this journey.

¶8 And eventually we're going to arrive at Allah (swt), why should we try to rush it forward so to speak, why should you try to do it in this world, rather than waiting for the time to come? And we go through we are actually taken through this journey by Allahs will rather than by our will. Is there any answer to this? Yes. The involuntary journey is longer and harder. It is yeah, yeah….. And also…... When people are going through that involuntary journey, these people have already completed the journey and already are living beside Allah (swt) and therefore Of course, there is more merits in this voluntary one rather than involuntary one. In this journey, there is no question of moving from one place to another, as we said, Neither does it refer to wayfarers movements in space know that of the destination ….

¶9 for God therfore is closer to a person than his own jugular vein, so God is here we are not going to go anywhere. However, we are going to, to sharpen our understanding to feel, here by journey is meant the removal of the veil that obstruct the vision of the heart and the light of divine acci….. from shining in the wayfarers heart. This is the same journey for which man has been created. So we actually have been created to see the glory, the beauty of Allah (swt) we will see it one day but it can take the veils from our heart. This is the surface of this journey to take the veils from the heart and how all these methods and techniques and different ways that Sufis have improvised in different religion is to sharpen the heart and to take the veil.

¶10 The veil, as we mentioned are dark veils and light veils, shining veils and of course, there are different types of practice at every stage to deal away with these to do away with these different veils which obstruct us from seeing the glory and beauty of the Lord. Now the Sufis say the first and foremost as the most important step that you have to take, of course after being awakened, that you are in a slumber when realizing that you in your slumber and you have to wake up is to repent. Repent of course is not repenting some things in a in a formal way, it is repenting from our casualness towards the Lord, first of all, repenting from taking everything for granted, repenting from wasting our lives and repenting from not taking heed of the presence of Allah(swt) and all the things which ordinarily we do not regard to these things, and we are not going to be punished for themselves.

¶11 But now you want to move a step up and for moving the step up of course, you have to have better qualifications. If you want a better job, you need a higher qualification. If you want a better station, you need a better state of mind state of behavior and for that you have to of course, repent, leave whatever you were doing, leave it behind and move forward. So the first step is, of course to repent. Now is a sinful person also qualifies? Usually the believers the momenoon when they want to move higher, they repent from what I said, and they saw a better life and they move higher. What about a sinner? What about someone who has done evil things in the last, can they step into this journey, can they start this journey, if they really repent from what they have done?

¶12 The answer is yes, because repentance is something which covers all the sin and covers all types of bad attitudes towards Allah (swt) and we have had some mystics, like for example, Bishr al hafi or like Fuzail bin ayaaz who were real mischievous people, and then, they came to their mind suddenly something struck a chord, in their mind in their soul, and they repented in a way that they wholeheartedly were absorbed into religion of God and then it is part of moving towards Allah(swt) and becoming a mystic.

¶13 Quest - Is it possible that, for example, if someone who is a sinner before they repent, and then through habits, they commit some sin, but they try and get rid of that isn't the same thing or do they have to since they have repented they cannot do anything?

¶14 Maulana - They might do it but I mean, if they want to go to that high, high station, they have to, to leave all these behind before they enter that. I mean, they have to really leave those ordinary things that ordinary people do before then they can come to this station of repenting from the things which people do not regard.

¶15 It might happen again, but they have to repent again, of course, it is a continuous process is a continuous problem fight, that's what is called mujahida, is a fight, is really a fight with one's own selves. And it is continous, at every stage, there is a danger that the self would come back and make take revenge and when it takes revenge in a very bad way it hits the person in the face in a way that for some day they are dizzy. Okay, what about repentance? The verse of the Quran ‘Qul yaa'ibaadiyal lazeena asrafoo 'alaaa anfusihim laa taqnatoo mirrahmatil laah; (sura39:ayat53). Now this qunoot, this being disappointed and in a, in a state of despair usually happens for all believers, I mean, of course, those who sin very much.

¶16 Sometimes they say we are such a sinner that there is no way for us to go back. Of course these people are much great in number. Usually everyone has hope that Allah is forgiving. This is something that we know about our instinct. Even if the prophet wouldn't have told us we know that Allah has forgiveness. Now, usually for us, when we want to go to a higher position, this situation of this path is more outstanding and more apparent. Usually ordinary believers say that we never can reach those stations and this is because they can judge their minds and they see that this is not for us, this is for people of higher caliber. And this is exactly what the verse is adressing.

¶17 You have wronged yourself, to your soul asrafoo alaaa’anfusihim’ now, this might mean real thing, but it gives more the feeling that those who have wasted lots of capacities in their souls and now they have become disappointed, to be able to move in this path. Of course, we are very strongly advised that do not be like that, never get disappointed from the Allah's mercy, because he produced all this. innal laaha yaghfiruz zunooba jamee'aa; innahoo Huwal Ghafoorur Raheem(sura39:ayat53) all these things and I think this is something which is very encouraging for the beginning of the of the way I mean you never say that me, to be such a simple person to be such a waste to be such an idle person.

¶18 How can I start? How would God accept me in this? He might forgive me, I might go to Jannah but to move on this path is impossible for me. This we have to put aside so laa taqnatoo mirrahmatil laah.

¶19 Quest -age is not a factor, I've talked to some people who are older and they've said that this is impossible.

¶20 Maulana - Ok this is taqnatoo rehmatullah, this is disappointment from rehmatullah

¶21 Quest – So after a certain age it would become much more difficult?

¶22 Maulana - It would become difficult but if there is a result and repentance and real struggle, it is possible. It is difficult I mean, it's difficult because you see, when you want to become a boxer or wrestler at a very young age, it's very easy. You can do but when you grow old, it is very difficult because your energy, your power, your capacities have actually diminished and therefore for spiritual things as well you will diminish in all damage. So it's very difficult when you become when you grow old but it is not impossible, if only your abilities which wouldn't allow you, it is not the mercy of God which could not reach use your ability to hear.

¶23 Quest - somebody heard somebody won't say that this is not a linear process. You can take many steps and not get very far. But there may be a few steps and you reach very far.

¶24 Maulana – That’s true if you know really what to do and how you use your life and how you use your ….rs. Otherwise, you might just a step here and then. Yeah, that's true. I mean, the right getting the right instruction is very important. Sometimes you do something very quickly and you want to come to the conclusion very quickly, and you arrive at something but this is not where you have to end. And I had an example this morning in my ethics class. A friend of mine just recently came from Iran he left today. He's the son of Ayatollah Amjad in Teheran probably have heard on he was a close associate of Ayatollah Bahauddin who passed away a few years ago and he was telling me that at one stage, he was young and he was feeling very heavy in his heart, very disappointed from lies, and lots of doubts coming to his heart, this son of that Ayatollah Amjad and someone advised him to take recourse with Ziyarate Ashura and he said I started to do the ziyarat every morning.

¶25 Of course, 100 laanat and 100 salam because the main purpose of the whole ziyarat is that hundred laanat and hundred salam and sometimes we just recited without that 100 laanat and salam, it's good but those things which are said about the effectiveness of this ziyarate Ashura is with that they are 100 laanat and 100 salam, he said I used to do it every day for a long time and gradually started to show its effect, I felt very better, I felt very much elated and even people could recognize that in my face. My face became very shown and people could see the light in my face. And I was very happy about that. Until one day Ayatollah Bahauddin came to our house and because he paid regular visits to Tehran, and whenever he came to Tehran, he went to their house and he saw me and he found, out well my face was showing that I was doing something some sort of practice which is affecting my spiritual status.

¶26 And he told my father what your son is doing. What is he doing? There is something he said yes, he's reciting ziyarate ashura every day and he told my father tell him to stop. And my father was amazed because he has advised me to do that. And when my father told me, I won't ever comment, it is why. And I asked him why he advised me to stop. I feel very good. And he says, because you need to have basis. You are rushing something you are pushing yourself forward very quick. And then suddenly, you might fall so you have to do it with some basis with a linear gradual improvement rather than say for example, fasting suddenly for three months, getting so much spiritual energy and then suddenly you feel that you're left abandoned by your own soul, because you cannot take it further.

¶27 It is very, very important to be to be aware of the dangers of rushing things forward and doing it according to the pace that our Aimmah have adviced is very, very important. Okay. So first of all, if someone wants to repent, there is no disappointment here. Everything can be done with the mercy of Allah subhanaw taala and his forgiveness … Wa izaa jaaa'akal lazeena yu'minoona bi Aayaatinaa faqul salaamun 'alaikum kataba Rabbukum 'alaa nafsihir rahmata(sura6:ayat54)… and when those who believe in our revelations come on to the say peace be unto you. Now, those people who are mentioned here are ordinary believers who do lots of things okay. And still they are believers like us. Okay. And the prophet is ordered to greet them with his greetings so when they come to you, say salamun alaykum to them, kataba rabbukum alaa nafsir rahmata, your Lord has prescribed for himself mercy and whoever have you have done patience especially they have done something wrong with ignorance.

¶29 Now I skipped the other hadees and ayats, there is a special instruction for repentance in Zilqadah. If you want inshallah to start sulook, and this is the high time today was the first of zilqadah, the prophets had instructed this type of repentance in zilqadah which is very effective actually, anyone who wants to come out of this ordinary stage now, on a Sunday of Zilqadah, Prophet came to the people this is reported in many books of hadees actually and if you put in Mafaatihul jinaan in muraagibaat of Maliki and others and especially, Mirza Maliki has advised this Maliki was a mystic one of the teachers of Imam Khomeini in mysticism. He has a special advice for those who want to start a better and deeper life in fiqh.

¶30 So, the Prophet came on a Sunday of Zilqadah and addressed the companion stated who wants to repent to God and of course, the companion said, all of them once said, we want to repent. And then the Prophet said that you do make Ghusl. Of course, it was a Sunday in Zilqadah that Prophet said but usually the traditionalist they say that you could do it at any time, but the high time is on a Sunday, in Zilqadah, the Prophet said do make ghusl and then make ablution make wudu after that. So the niyyat for this ghusl is, Ghusle Tauba and then perform four rakaats of Salah and in each rakaat you do one you recite one Surah Fatiha, 3 Surah Ikhlaas and once Surah Naas, and then say Istighfar 70 times, astagfirullah rabbi watoobo ilayhe, the exact phrase is not mentioned in the riwayat, it just says do 70 times astagfaar after these four rakaats, and of course the four rakaats are done in twos.

¶31 Every mustahab salaats are done in twos.

¶32 And then say la hawla walaa quwwat illa billa and then say Ya Azzezo Ya Ghaffaar, igfirli zunoobi wa zonuuba jameean wal momennena wal momenaat fa innahu laa yagferuz zonuuba illa ant.

¶33 Now then, there's a long list given by the Prophet whoever does the Salah, istigfaar and actually do Tauba in this way then an angel would call from the heavens that all servants of God owes, you be happy because all your sins and the sin of your descendants and sin of your parents are forgiven and another angel will say that. Re start whatever you want to do because you are completely clear, another angel would call something just another, there is a long list of any of what Prophet actually mentioned about this and of course it is not amazing when God forgives people in a way that the blessings pour from every direction. And so this is the first step Sunday inshallah.

¶44 Now it says oh Muhammad, I have just put some statements from the Hadees here on the Powerpoint, my love encompasses those who love for my sake. It means when they love someone they love them because of me. Even if they love someone who is very sinful, they love them because they are creatures of God. Because God still have some hope in them so we should still have some hope in them. And because of course the relationship is for God it is always the case that it wouldn't turn into those type of relations which always come with quarrel agitation, and also they love for me, it means that they love the faithful more than the sinners.

¶45 Because the more they find my light in someone, the more they love them. So they are, they love for my sake. And those who show compassion for my sake and those who hold associations for my sake and those who rely on there's no signpost or boundary or limit to my love. So it means that when Allah loves someone, there's no limit for it you cannot imagine how far he could take them. “And whenever I remove one sign I placed for them another in, in the field of my love there are these are the ones who regard the people the way I regard and they never ask for the need from others, their relationship is based on Allahs way, not because they need the people they form in relationship is because of God that they form a relationship as we have been looked on.

¶46 He says” O Ahmad I swear by my might and honor if a certain servant results to apply for qualities for my sake, I will certainly enter him into paradise to see his calm and not opening it except in what concerns him to safe guard his heart from temptation to be mindful that I'm aware of his acts and I'm watching him to take hunger as his life”, which are very important the third the statement “to be mindful that I'm aware of this and I am watching him”, is something with the mystics called Al muraaqabah means to be watchful and to be watchful and mindful of presence of God and that God is looking and seeing. And this hadees is often repeated by the mystics “worship God as you see him, and if you do not see him know that he is seeing you and this is the state of muraaqabah.

¶47 Maybe you remember from Imam Khomeini he usually used to advise the politicians, his politicians actually, that this world is the place of presence of manifests manifestation of Allah. He used to say that this is where Allah is present, he was really seeing. And this is what is called muraaqabah, to feel that Allah is here and is watching. This is very important, of course.

¶48 How is that different from taqwa?

¶49 Taqwa is that you really refrain from disobeying God, even without feeling his presence. Of course it is a deeper level of taqwa. But when it gets very, very thick, when the taqwa gets very strong, it gives you this sense of muraaqabah all the time, all the time you feel Allah is around and therefore it restrains you completely from either idle thinking, because you feel that Allah is around, you are watchful of His presence.

¶50 The second statement, one of the most difficult paths of mystical practice that mystics mentioned that you keep your heart and your mind from, idle imagination from wishes, the chain of thought, it is usually the chain of thoughts, which drags us into sin. You imagine something and you imagine that you want it then you imagine how can I get it? And then you imagine ways that you could actually improvised ways that you can go and get it. And then even if it is haram, you say no, or I mean, it diverts you from ibadah from everything. So all these temptations, waswaas coming to the mind, which the mystic say you have to block, in order to be able to divert your attention to Allah subhanaw taala, it is of course very difficult as well, but the first and the last are somehow preparations for these two, of course, it's not put in an orderly way.

¶51 I'm just explaining in a mystical order, that silence and hunger, these are the 2 prequisites you get that state of muraaqabah and you get that power to block imaginations, attacking your mind and when the mind becomes clean, or when the heart becomes clean even the imagination become clean and this is why mystics usually say and they prove that the infallible, the Aimmah , the Masumeens even their talk is masum, never vicious thoughts attack the mind or attack the heart, it is blocked, even whatever they think is masum. And therefore whatever they dream because dream usually we are taken into a world which we deserve in dream. Okay. Now, in dream as well they see only things which are clean and pure.

¶52 And this is why they say that when a Prophet is given the Prophethood whatever they dream is revelation, so the dream of the Prophet is revelation, there's no doubt and actually the Quran mentions the dream of our Prophet as being revelation like for example, he dreamt that monkeys were jumping on his pockets. And Quran mentioned that this riwayat was right and he says ‘wa maa ja'alnar ru'yal lateee arainaaka illaa fitnatal linnaasi washshajaratal mal'oonata fil quraan; (sura17:ayat 60) We granted a vision which we showed you, and this is just a tribulation for the piece I have mentioned is a tribulation for the people. Laqad sadaqal laahu Rasoolahur ru'yaa bilhaqq latadkhulunnal Masjidal-Haraama in shaaa'al laahu aamineena,(sura fath:ayat 27) muhalliqeena ru'oosakum wa muqassireena laa takhaafoona fa'alima maa lam ta'lamoo faja'ala min dooni zaalika fathan qareebaa, the same way that the prophets had. ¶54 So the dream of the Prophet is revelation. Why? because these currents of vile imagination which usually attack one wouldn't attack them.

And now, let's discuss these issues which have come up as well in the in this hadith of Meraj.

¶59 In the hadith of Meraj you have Allahs silence. So O Ahmad(pbuh) adopt silence because the most flourishing heart out of those who are virteous from silence and the most barren hearts of those who indulge in vain and idle speech, means to talk about things which are of no concern which is not related. And this is the criteria I mean, entering discussions talking about an issue or even preaching people in some sort of manner, which is not our business, this will not concern us which will not benefit us and others is the type of silence that we are advised to keep, do not talk, only talk about things which would benefit others and also would concern you because I mean in our daily life we have to speak to I mean if we were to keep silent all the time, why Allah has given us this tongue and these vocal cords and all these things, it is there for a purpose, to speak of course, but do not speak what is not of your concern and what is other people's business, and what would not benefit you and others, this is the type of silence that you are actually required to keep.(inaudible)

When I say this I don't mean that it applies to everyone, I mean, it might be beneficial for some of us, we don't know. That was just a special instance of a person who was in a specific situation. But yeah, certainly even if you reach some mystical if you find some mystical experiences, but you cannot justify it you just become bewildered. You cannot analyze it in terms of what because we see these things I mean, these mystical experiences, especially at the beginning, they come in adversity, they come without our control, and we see things that we cannot explain it.

¶61 And this might lead us either to madness or to being presumptuous, or to become arrogant unless you can explain them according to what the prophets and Imams have said. I have an instance of someone which sees many different things from aalame barzakh and she is on the verge of madness because she cannot explain it. It's just inadvertently just a gift but she cannot she had no knowledge whatsoever. And this is why usually these people are called schizophrenic. They go mad they do unsaid things, because they cannot explain. So yeah, it's very important. Of course, to have this type of behavior is important. Also to have knowledge, base of knowledge which is very important, and that knowledge doesn't come through mystical experience.

¶62 You have to learn that.

¶63 Quest – I read a book about Shk Rajabali. He was not an arif but he was a learned person. He used to control his nafs he had that gift.

¶64 Maulana - knowledge was given to him although not through the book, but through relationship with Olama and sometimes they are given with knowledge. Sometimes they are given without knowledge and if one practices whatever the Prophet says, they come with knowledge with some sort of deep knowledge which is taught by Allah subhanaw taala. But sometimes these experiences come without that knowledge, and this is when people go mad.

¶65 Now hunger. Again in that hadith we have the Prophet asking the Lord, My Lord, what is the benefit of hunger? He replied, wisdom, in ramadhan like we see that wisdom sometimes.

¶66 Quest - There is ahadees of Imam jafare sadiq (as) saying knowledge is best achieved on an empty stomach.

¶67 Maulana -Of course, the important thing is that wisdom and knowledge doesn't come with filled stomach. But not always hunger will give wisdom. But if you want wisdom, you have to have lighter stomach, this is very important.

¶68 Quest – What is Hikmah and shed their body whenever they want it?

¶69 Maulana - Shedding the body is you mean the soul leaving the body? Whatever they want, whenever they want. And then when we sleep we do that, isn't it? I mean, all people are capable of doing it inadvertntly. Now the only thing is that you want to get control over it. Yes, it's possible, it's possible to get control over it but it is not something very amazing. It's not against the physical nature of human beings because we do it every night. The only thing is that we do not think about these processes happening. Allah takes the soul when you sleep and when you die. So it happens every day and every night for us. The only things they want to bring it onto your control, and some people can, just like digestion you cannot control it, but some people can.

¶70 I have seen it and they have the stomach under their control. And I saw one someone from the Qadri silsila of Sufis, he swallowed a very, very big stone. I think it was twice this cup. And he didn't have teeth here. That's why we could just tuck it in his mouth. Otherwise the song wouldn't have gone in, it was so big and he swallowed it. And then he just willed to bring it back. So the stomach was under his control. Now if you can do that, if you can get your stomach under your control. You can get your sleep under control and your soul leaving your body and coming back. This is not something which is very much I mean, it's just getting uncontrollable practices of the soul and body under your control.

¶71 Bring it under control. Ah okay, what is the benefit of hunger and he replied, wisdom and protection of the heart and proximity to me and constant sadness. Of course, this is the whole rule which the heart has when thinks about Allah subhanaw taala the type of grief which the heart feels being separated from Allah (swt) and needing it live probably and among the people and truthful speech and indifference to whether life is hard or easy. Or Ahmad do you know when a servant appears proximity to God, he said no my Lord and he said when he's either in a state of hunger or in prostration now, here, Allah has actually made hunger parallel to prostration which is the most manifest acts of worship.

¶72 Now, what do we mean by this hunger? I mean certainly even when we fast we fast for a very limited period, especially if you fast nowadays and just 6.30 to 4, so it's very limited. You don't feel that much hunger and of course we eat when we break fast. However, this hunger, of course, there are different levels of it. But what is meant here is that you never should be unease, it is very important. If you feel unease when you eat it means that all your attention the attention of the soul is directed to do something with this stomach which is filled with different things somehow to sort things out. So you eat in a way that you don't feel heavy, never, because if you feel heavy, the mind goes dizzy and you cannot remember God.

¶73 You cannot pray well. So the most important thing is that you should not feel heavy. Never, when you saw this hadees that we have a momin would stop eating when they can eat 40 more morsels. So I don't know how many most of you eat in a portion of food, but when you stop eating you can you have to be able to eat another 40 morsel before you get filled up. And there's another of course benefits for this and that's because if afterwards you are invited somewhere else you can have another morsel.

¶74 Then he asked my Lord, what is the essence of worship? He says the essence of worship is silence and this is what mystics at the beginning especially some tariqas they are advice silence for continuous days and of course fasting for continuous days. And it was a practice before our religion that people had fast of silence you have heard in the Quran. fa immaa tarayinnna minal bashari ahadan faqooleee innee nazartu lir Rahmaani sawman (sura 19 :ayat 26) it was a habit in banu israiil. Among the monks that they did, they had fast of silence they fasted from speaking and they don't speak several days to anyone. And if there was a sign that they signed to people that we have a fast of silence, I will not speak and this is how Maryam was adviced, not to tell anything.

¶75 When you see anyone, you sign to them that you have a fast of silence and you do not speak to anyone. Today, I will not speak with anyone it means that probably the shortest period of this fast of silence was one day. She could not break it until the end of the day. And this is how it is said here. The first of the worship is silence and fasting. He asked my Lord and what is the benefit of fasting? He stated fasting gives rise to wisdom again, the same thing and wisdom gives rise to godly knowledge, maarefa and godly knowledge gives rise to certitude, yaqeen. So when a servant attains certitude he no longer cares how he passes his days and nights whether in ease or in harsh, again the same thing the benefits of eating and speaking less, O Ahmad when a servant remains hungry and guards his tongue, then I teach him wisdom.

¶76 And what is the relation between these we dont know but mystics have experienced. There is an outcome for that and that is wisdom. Then if such a person is an unbeliever you see, there is an outcome on whether the believer or non believer this wisdom will become a witness against him and hashr and if he is a believer, then his wisdom will become for him. And illumination, a logical reason healing and mercy and he will know what he did not know before and he will see what he did not see before. The first thing that I will show him will be his own thoughts now this is very interesting isn't it. The beginning of wisdom is when you see wrong before he gets involved with the faults of others, and I will show you the details of knowledge so that shaytaan cannot be…….

¶77 very interesting, isn't it? And of course it's very difficult as well. Now, you remember, this hadith of Imam Jafare Sadiq(as) speaking to Unwan al Basri, I think this is a good explanation of this silence and hunger and wisdom and Basri was a very old man, of course, it's sunni, he wanted some knowledge from Jafare Sadiq. At the beginning he was rejected and Imam told him that I'm busy you better go to Malik, Malik ibne anas and other people in Medina there are lots of scholars here go and learn from them. Because of course he was not that level that Imam could teach him something. But he went to Allah that Allah would soften the heart of Imam Jafar, as he said, soften the heart of Jafar to me so that he could teach me something.

¶78 And when he went back Imam Jafar, of course received him very warmly and he started to advise him a few things. Firstly, adviced on self discipline from Basri, he says firstly, do not eat that which you have no… Of course, these are the beginning of that fasting and hunger that mystics should observe, for this brings about the idiocy and stupidity is clear. I mean, if you don't have appetite for something and you just waste, waste of money, waste of food, waste of our stomach waste of energy. Secondly, do not eat unless you're hungry because usually we eat out of habit. We have to eat breakfast, lunch and dinner whatever we are hungry or no. So this is not a good habit.

¶79 Do not eat unless you're hungry. Tell me when you do eat, eat only that which is no Halal, lawful and begin in the name of Allah and remind yourself of the tradition of the Prophet (sa) there is no vessel that man fills above the allowed level worse than his own stomach. This is a very famous Hadith from the Prophet. So if you must fill it then allow 1/3 of his food another third for drink and keep last 3rd for air. Because usually people just do the whole three parts with food. They don't care about water or air.

¶80 Quest - I have a question what if we don’t like vegetables? Like chocolates like some delicious nice, very rich foods and you don't have your appetite for healthy food for example exactly like me I like biryani or whatever not so keen on vegetables .My mum asked me what would I tell, my kids they don't eat their greens if someone wants to invite us?

¶81 Maulana -Well of course, kids usually are very choicy in eating. They cannot actually judge what is good for them what is bad for them, it is usually moms who should tell them you have to eat this is a different situation certainly for a grown up person. Anyhow look at it in slightly different lighting the next week actually discussing food in general. When you are hungry you eat a banana or you eat biryani as long as you take these points into consideration that you do not eat so much that you do not breathe after the event.(1:11:11 inaudible) till (1:11:35)

¶82 Quest -I don't know but I never eat garlic. Good for your back. On that point, I remember people talk about Imam Alis time and sometimes the bread was so hard because it was harder than sometimes. People thought it was like rock Yeah. But then he says to people don't follow this because you can't do it. Can you explain that please?

¶83 Maulana -Well he's in level 1000 we just want to start level one. And this is this is instruction for level one. So he was telling people not to imitate him. Yeah. Because of course that level was not something that could be imitated by anyone.

¶84 Usually Of course, every bit of food would have probably enough nourishment. Now of course, the scientists would have divided schools with different types of vitamins and all these things but probably the amount of these things in everything. There might be a little or more but the type of nourishment the body needs probably is there in that piece of bread is only the case of our body cannot use that type of nourishment. It's not used to it cannot use that tiny bits of different things. But for a trained body trained soul it is possible to get the best of nourishment out of that as it is self explanatory, you ask why eating such a food? How could you have such power to fight in those battles?

¶85 And then he said, you look at a tree which which grows in the desert and tree which grows beside the river, which one is stronger, certainly the tree which grows in the desert because that tree knows how to use the nourishment of that barren land but a tree in a garden, it is used to very easy type of getting provisions.

¶86 Qust -Is it something like that too much meat makes your heart hard?

¶87 Maulana - It is said as well and that's why you shouldn't eat probably meat twice a day and advisable that you eat meat every other day not every day. It is I mean we have many hadees about this but leaving meat altogether would be other difficulties even spiritual difficulties. Now we see some advice with clemency from Imam Sadiq to Unwan al Basri, he mentioned about the husnus seerat. Firstly, it actually relates to silence as well and keeping your tongue firstly if someone were to say to you, if you dare say a word, I will give you 10 back then you shouldn't be such as to reply even if you say 10 words you will not hear a single one that is actually keeping the tongue.

¶88 Secondly, when someone insults you, do not get angry and do not try to insult them. Say if you're right in what you say you are saying that may Allah forgive you. For example, if someone is angry with you then for example in a business or something they think that you have wronged them while you haven't and they say you are a robber. I mean, you just say what if you are right may God forgive me and you know that right? And if you're wrong, then maybe forgive you for being wrong and same and thirdly when someone feels too harsh, you return it with good counsel and pray for him. And this is of course that good manner which we discussed about husnus seerat and also the way you have your tongue with regards to others.

¶89 Now Inshallah, then we'll talk about night vigil on Friday or Sunday .
